assumptions: The /transl_table qualifier, or the record's default, is the code the CDS uses.
limits: Partial ends and /pseudo CDS are not judged.
A flag says the annotation and the bases disagree, not which one is wrong.
bio.jane/contract.question: Does every annotated CDS of a map translate cleanly from its own bases and genetic code?

description: Check every annotated CDS of one or more GenBank maps against its own bases and genetic code: a frame that does not close (frameshift), a stop inside the reading frame, a first codon the code cannot start with, a last codon that is not a stop, and a /translation the bases do not give. A partial end (< or >) is not judged, and a /pseudo CDS carries no flag. Where an annotation ends without a stop it reads on in frame (round the origin of a circular map) to the first stop and says how many codons that adds, whether it runs into another annotated CDS (a fusion annotated in pieces) and the read-through a random backbone of the same composition would give. Extraction and translation match Biopython on all 1,871 CDS of 695 NCBI vector records.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

genbank.description: the GenBank files' contents, one string per file (a file may hold several records).
